contract_findings: The pass holds P4 vocabulary only: shoulder insertions, elbow and knee transitions, wrist/ankle bridges, hand and boot blocks, hip-to-thigh insertions and prop attachment/overlap.
No shading, texture, decorative detail, clothing folds or facial features were introduced, and the P1 gesture, P2 axes and P3 masses are all preserved.
drawing_findings: boots_ground: both boot blocks register with the subject's boots, attach to their ankles rather than floating, and preserve the differing sole heights that carry the support-versus-brace reading.

knee_ankle: a real defect. The knee planes span roughly 169-197 and 268-300 while the leg masses there span 166-199 and 262-301, so both read as full-width stripes across the leg rather than partial directional planes. Both ankle bridges have the same problem.
shoulder_elbow: the same defect on the near elbow, whose transition spans 279-299 across a sleeve that spans 280-300.
shoulder_elbow: the shoulder insertions themselves are correct partial curves that carry the arm out of the torso.

hand_pocket: the hand block registers with the subject's glove but is authored as a closed faceted blob, which reads as a mitten polygon rather than as a smooth wrist-to-palm volume cut off by the pocket.
The hip-to-thigh insertions duplicate the P3 shorts hems at nearly full width, adding a second parallel band instead of explaining the insertion.
Fresh residual sweep: no joint requires moving a P3 mass, so this is a P4 authoring problem and does not justify reopening upstream.
exemplar_findings: The bundled P4 grammar exemplar carries a KNOWN AUDIT FAILURE for under-explained structural transitions, so it was used only for detail budget and not as a model for how to connect masses.
observations: The pass holds P4 vocabulary only: shoulder insertions, elbow and knee transitions, wrist/ankle bridges, hand and boot blocks, hip-to-thigh insertions and prop attachment/overlap.
No shading, texture, decorative detail, clothing folds or facial features were introduced, and the P1 gesture, P2 axes and P3 masses are all preserved.
The subject's boots are two distinct grounded volumes whose soles land at different heights, and both toes swing image-right.
The subject's near hand disappears into the hip pocket, so only a partial wrist-to-palm volume is actually visible.
The subject's joints are hidden under loose clothing everywhere except the bare thigh, so only functional transitions are observable, never anatomical joint shapes.
